The test image shows:
- Tomato stem pulled from soil, split open longitudinally
- White cottony/mycelial growth visible at the stem base near the soil line
- Internal stem tissue showing brown discoloration
- Plant wilted/dead with dried leaves
- Sandy soil context

White mycelium at the soil line strongly suggests **Southern Blight** (Sclerotium rolfsii). Let me check one reference image.

The reference image shows Southern Blight field symptom (collapsed tomato plants), and the test image shows the close-up of a pulled stem with white mycelial growth at the soil line — the hallmark of Sclerotium rolfsii (Southern Blight). Both images share the same Bugwood 156XXXX series. The white cottony mycelium at the stem base, combined with internal stem rot and plant collapse, is diagnostic.
